items.title: Tom Brown Interview, 1956
items.q: I've made over 100 recordings with Johnny Wiggs that I think are very good.

ctx.x: Well, Art, they all say that I was the one that took the first Dixieland band to Chicago.

So it must be so. This band was later turned into jazz by Chicago local musicians. Well, we had the finest kind of tempo and rhythm that took the world by surprise and started something really big. That it is all over the world today. I've enjoyed the fruits of jazz since 1950. I made a lot of photograph records which have made hits. I've made some good records with Yerkes. Yerkes, Dance Orchestra. Yerkes, Happy Six. Yerkes, Southern Five. Yerkes, Jazz Marimba Orchestra. Ray Miller's Black and White Melody Boys.…

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: And Tom Brown played in my band, and Eddie Chance played in my band.

ctx.x: My feeling is that I've interviewed a lot of these people. I'm fortunate enough to interview Papa Lane several times. But you go to books, you go to all these different sources, and you always seem to be at least one step away. You talk to Papa Lane, and he tells you about his older brothers. Well, what do we know about Buddy Bolden, who came before him? And it's just you never can quite get to the exact truth. What the historians say is that history is a tattered cloak. And there are many different opinions. If…

Yeah. Well, I heard most of the Negro bands were considered marching bands. Like, I heard that Papa Lane was a marching band, and not a jazz band, it's so-called. And I was wondering, do you have any information on this? Well, he was, his band was made up of people that played by ear. Now, ear music usually comes out what we call jazz, or ragtime. In the early days, it was ragtime-ish, and it has changed, and it has become more fluid in recent times. It's beginning, as far as I'm concerned, when I heard Joe…

Well, thank you, Johnny, very much. That's very flattering. But what I've done is collect these things, along with a lot of other people, and it's been a cooperative thing. And we were fortunate enough to have the help of Mrs. Tom Brown, who let us copy a tape interview with Tom Brown. And she gave us a lot of information. And, of course, we have old magazines, various jazz histories and books that have information on Tom Brown. And Eddie Chance can help you.
